records.people: Swee Lian Teo (Teo Swee Lian) (Monetary Authority of Singapore, over 27 years, rising to Deputy Managing Director for Financial Supervision; retired 2015 as Special Advisor in the Managing Director's office; appointed to the board of HSBC Holdings plc on 1 October 2023)
records.move: from Deputy Managing Director for Financial Supervision at the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and Special Advisor in the Managing Director's office until her retirement in 2015, to the board of directors of HSBC Holdings plc on 1 October 2023
records.years: MAS career of over 27 years, retired 2015; HSBC Holdings plc board from 1 October 2023
records.summary: HSBC's own board biography page states that Swee Lian Teo spent over 27 years at the Monetary Authority of Singapore in foreign reserves management, financial sector development, strategic planning and financial supervision, rose to Deputy Managing Director for Financial Supervision and retired in 2015 as Special Advisor in the Managing Director's office, and that she was appointed to the HSBC Holdings plc board on 1 October 2023. The private side is HSBC Holdings plc, the publicly traded holding company of the HSBC banking group and a bank holding company in its own right rather than a subsidiary of any group; the biography page itself does not state its ownership or listing, and that is said here rather than asserted. The page also lists her earlier non-executive directorships at AIA Group Limited and at Clifford Capital Private Limited and Clifford Capital Holdings Private Limited. Distinct from the Singapore record the map already holds, which is Ong Chong Tee moving from MAS Deputy Managing Director to the board of United Overseas Bank: different person, different firm, different source.
records.source_title: Swee Lian Teo — Board of Directors, HSBC Holdings plc

records.people: Matilda Asante-Asiedu (Group Head of Retail Banking at Access Bank (Ghana) PLC; appointed second Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana, reported 28 April 2025)
records.move: from Group Head of Retail Banking at Access Bank (Ghana) PLC to second Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana
records.years: at Access Bank from May 2010 (Head of Corporate Communications and Brand Management to June 2015, later Head of Exclusive Banking and Group Head of Retail Banking); appointment to the Bank of Ghana reported 28 April 2025
records.summary: The Daily Graphic reports that Matilda Asante-Asiedu has been appointed second Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana, in a statement by Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Minister of State for Government Communications, and describes her as Group Head of Retail Banking at Access Bank (Ghana) PLC. The article sets out her earlier career: journalist at Joy FM from 1997 to 2009, consultant to international organisations, then Head of Corporate Communications and Brand Management at Access Bank from May 2010 to June 2015 and later Head of Exclusive Banking. The private side is Access Bank (Ghana) PLC, a commercial bank operating in Ghana; the article names the bank and says she moved into the banking sector there but does not state its ownership, shareholders or listing, so no ownership claim is made here and the record rests only on the employer being a named commercial bank. The date given, 28 April 2025, is the article's own publication date, which is the date on which the article reports the statement; no separate decree date appears on the page.
records.source_title: Matilda Asante-Asiedu appointed BoG deputy Governor — Graphic Online

records.people: Christian Hawkesby (senior member of the Harbour Asset Management team, Wellington; appointed Assistant Governor and General Manager of Economics, Financial Markets and Banking at the Reserve Bank of New Zealand from 18 March 2019)
records.move: from the Wellington-based Harbour Asset Management team, where he was head of fixed income, to Assistant Governor and General Manager of Economics, Financial Markets and Banking at the Reserve Bank of New Zealand from 18 March 2019
records.years: eight years at Harbour Asset Management to early 2019; Reserve Bank post from 18 March 2019
records.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's own news release announcing two appointments to its senior leadership team states that Christian Hawkesby joins as Assistant Governor and General Manager of Economics, Financial Markets and Banking from 18 March 2019, and that he comes from the Wellington-based Harbour Asset Management team in the competitive asset management industry, after earlier work at the Reserve Bank as a graduate and at the Bank of England, where he was Head of Market Intelligence during the global financial crisis. The private side is Harbour Asset Management, a funds management firm; the release describes it only as a Wellington-based asset manager and does not state its ownership, shareholders or listing, so no ownership claim is made here. His title and length of service at Harbour, head of fixed income and eight years, come from a second source named here, the trade report 'Hawkesby exits Harbour for RBNZ' published by Investment News NZ on 14 January 2019, which likewise states nothing about Harbour's ownership. Distinct from the New Zealand record the map holds for Adrian Orr. OWNERSHIP, added by the curator on 17 November 2026: neither the RBNZ release nor the Investment News report states who owns Harbour, which on this row settles nothing by itself. Harbour Asset Management Limited's own Other Material Information document, lodged on the New Zealand Disclose register, states that its ultimate holding company is Jarden Group Limited, formerly First NZ Capital Holdings Limited, and that 'The ultimate parent, Jarden Group Limited, is 100% privately owned by directors, management and employees of that business. There are 125 shareholders in Jarden Group Limited, with the largest shareholder owning more than 10% of the business.' That is the employer's own regulatory filing. DATE GAP STATED PLAINLY: the copy read is dated 1 July 2020 and the move was March 2019, so it is the nearest filing after the move and describes the Jarden ownership structure that existed then; Harbour was folded into the FirstCape group, jointly owned by National Australia Bank, Jarden and Pacific Equity Partners, only in 2024, which is after this record's period and is not what it rests on.
records.source_title: Two appointments complete RBNZ senior leadership team — Reserve Bank of New Zealand

records.people: Shyamala Gopinath (Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India for seven years and a member of its Board; part-time non-executive Chairperson of HDFC Bank Limited for a three-year term effective 2 January 2015)
records.move: from Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and member of its Board to part-time non-executive Chairperson of HDFC Bank Limited, for a three-year term effective 2 January 2015
records.years: HDFC Bank chairmanship from 2 January 2015; the RBI deputy governorship is given only as seven years, with no dates on either page
records.summary: HDFC Bank's own 'Profiles of Directors' page states that Mrs Gopinath has over 39 years of experience in financial sector policy formulation in different capacities at the RBI and that she served as Deputy Governor of the RBI for seven years and a member of the Board, and lists her at the bank as part-time non-executive Chairperson. Neither that page nor the second source named here gives dates for the RBI roles, so none is stated. The date and term come from that second source, a Business Standard report dated 2 January 2015, which says she was appointed part-time non-executive Chairperson of the bank for a three-year term effective 2 January 2015, approved by shareholders by postal ballot and by the Reserve Bank of India. The private side is HDFC Bank Limited; neither page calls it a private sector bank or states its shareholders, and the bank's own page says only that it ranks among the top 10 Indian banks by market capitalisation, which indicates a company listed in its own right rather than a subsidiary. That is the whole evidence of its character here and no ownership claim beyond it is made. Distinct from the three Indian records the map holds, for Rajan, Patel and Subbarao.
records.source_title: Profiles of Directors — HDFC Bank, Corporate Governance

blanks.read: MAR: Le360 (fr.le360.ma), 'Le Conseil de Bank Al-Maghrib fait peau neuve: decouvrez les nouveaux membres', read in full. It names all six incoming members of the Bank Al-Maghrib council and their prior posts: Mounssif Aderkaoui (UM6P professor, ex-director of studies at the Ministry of Economy and Finance), Jilali Kenzi (senior civil servant, ex-Inspector General of Finance, ex-deputy director of the Treasury and External Finance Directorate, career begun in 1985 at the Office des changes), Bouchra Rahmouni (UM6P professor), Fouzi Mourji (Universite Hassan II professor, eight years 1986-1993 in the Finance Minister's office), Abdelhak Senhadji (ex-deputy director of the IMF's Fiscal Affairs Department) and Raja Chakir (research director at INRAE, a French public research body). Not one of the six is described as coming from a bank, an insurance company or any private financial firm, so this appointment round yields no counted career move. The article dates the outgoing members' terms ending to a Head of Government decision of 30 April published in the Bulletin officiel and gives no appointment date for the new members. Vein not yet tried for Morocco: CVs of directors of Moroccan commercial banks (Attijariwafa, BMCE/Bank of Africa, Credit du Maroc under Holmarcom) for ex-Bank Al-Maghrib officials, and Bank Al-Maghrib's own direction-level biographies.

KHM: ACLEDA Bank Plc. annual report 2025 (ABC_Annual_Report_2025_Eng_SERC.pdf, acledasecurities.com.kh, first 100,000 of about 500,000 characters, which covers the governance sections) read for director and management career histories: the board section gives only names, positions and term dates and the executive management table only names, genders and positions, so the report carries no career histories at all and names nobody from the National Bank of Cambodia. The report does settle ACLEDA's ownership, listing five substantial shareholders - ACLEDA Financial Trust 28.3251 per cent, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation 18.0669 per cent, COFIBRED 12.1271 per cent, ORIX Corporation 12.1271 per cent and Shareholders Legalised from ASA, Plc. 5.7524 per cent - and records 'CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDER (30% OR MORE): N/A', which would settle the private-ownership leg for any career move found. One individual director biography page was then read, ff_bod_Chhay_Soeun: Chhay Soeun, Chairman, board member since August 2014, ACLEDA Bank from January 1993 to his retirement in April 2014 as Executive Vice President and Group Chief Financial Officer, and before that accountant and deputy chief accountant at the Kampot Provincial Department of Commerce 1980-1992 - no central bank post. Vein still open: the other ff_bod_* and ff_mgt_* biography pages on the same host, which are dated CVs one per person and are the resource that produced the Chea Sok record the map already holds.

ROU: a real candidate was found and could not be read. Profit.ro carries 'Rasvan Radu, care a condus UniCredit Romania aproape 18 ani, va fi consilierul de strategie al guvernatorului Isarescu' - on its headline, the man who ran UniCredit Romania for nearly 18 years becoming strategy adviser to the National Bank of Romania's governor, which would be a move from a listed private banking group into the central bank and is nobody in the Romanian record the map holds (Nicolae Danila, Banca Comerciala Romana to the NBR board). The page was fetched twice in this round and failed both times with a client error, so nothing of it was read and no record is filed on a headline alone. Next round: retry that profit.ro URL, or economica.net's 'Rasvan Radu pleaca de la sefia UniCredit Romania dupa 18 ani in pozitia de CEO a bancii' for the UniCredit side and the NBR's own site or Monitorul Oficial for the adviser appointment. Also unopened: bnr.ro/uploads/editor/1954215522.pdf, returned by the same search, and the Romanian Academy CV PDF format that produced the existing Danila record (aosr.ro), which suggests other board members' CVs exist in the same series.

ARE: searched for the post-governorship career of Mubarak Rashed Al Mansoori, Governor of the Central Bank of the UAE until 2021, since the record the map holds is the move in the other direction (Abdulhamid Saeed, First Abu Dhabi Bank to Governor, 2020). The only subsequent appointment the search surfaced, across the UAE Government Media Office, gpssa.gov.ae, Khaleej Times and Gulf News, is his appointment on 31 July 2023 as Chairman of the Board of Directors of the General Pension and Social Security Authority - a statutory state pension authority, which the brief classes as a state body, so even if filed it would be a public_move and would not count for this row. No page was opened, so the appointment itself is unverified here. Vein for the UAE: board and management biographies published by the Emirates' own listed banks (First Abu Dhabi Bank, Emirates NBD, Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank) for former central bank officials, which the map has not been tried on.

UGA: one search run on the phrase pattern that works on this row ('Bank of Uganda' former executive director, 'prior to joining', commercial bank board) and no document opened, so Uganda has not actually been tested. The search returned Ugandan commercial banks that publish board and management biographies on their own sites - Standard Chartered Uganda board and management committee pages, NCBA Group Uganda directors page, KCB Uganda, dfcu, Centenary Bank, Bank of Baroda Uganda - which is exactly the resource type this row converts on, plus a Makerere Endowment Fund trustee-profiles PDF that carries full dated career histories of Ugandan financial figures. None was fetched. The record the map holds is Stephen Mpuuga Kaboyo, Bank of Uganda to Alpha Capital Partners, so any of those board pages naming a different ex-Bank of Uganda official would be a second episode.

BWA: no search or fetch spent. Budget went to the five countries that converted plus the Morocco, Cambodia and Romania documents. Named lead for the next round: Bank of Botswana's own governor and deputy governor biographies and the board pages of Botswana's listed banks (Absa Bank Botswana, Standard Chartered Bank Botswana, First National Bank Botswana), all of which publish director CVs; the existing Botswana record is Linah Mohohlo moving from the governorship to the IMF, which is a public move, so a private-finance leg for any Bank of Botswana official would be the country's first counted one.

JOR: no search or fetch spent. The existing Jordanian record came from a commercial bank's own board page (Islamic International Arab Bank, iiabank.com.jo/en/page/board-directors, Mohammed Said Shahin), which shows the resource exists in English for Jordan; the same page type on Arab Bank, Jordan Kuwait Bank, Bank al Etihad, Capital Bank and Jordan Ahli Bank has not been read for other former Central Bank of Jordan governors or deputy governors, and Jordanian banks' annual corporate-governance reports carry director CVs alongside the shareholder table.

checked_not_in_assignment: None. No country outside the 29 in the assignment was researched. Two names surfaced incidentally while grepping the files rather than while searching, and neither was worked: KEN, whose existing revolving-door record already carries an Ecobank directorship (Sheila M'mbijjewe), found when grepping have_rd.json for 'Ecobank' to check whether the Ghana Ecobank lead would duplicate a firm already on the map; and PAK, named in the assignment only as a worked example, which the assignment itself says already holds two records so a further one would add no place. party_names.json was grepped before writing any employer name: it already carries 'HSBC', 'HSBC Bank USA, N.A.', 'Harbour Asset Management', 'ACLEDA Bank Plc.', 'United Overseas Bank', 'UniCredit S.p.A.', 'UniCredit Bank Hungary Zrt.', 'Ecobank Transnational Incorporated' and 'Access Bank (SL) Limited' - so the Singapore record's employer is written as the map's existing 'HSBC' spelling in substance while keeping HSBC's own wording 'HSBC Holdings plc', and 'Access Bank (Ghana) PLC' is kept distinct from the Sierra Leone entity already on the map. 'FBC Holdings' and 'HDFC Bank' are new names on the map.
leads_not_opened: GHA second candidate, not opened: myjoyonline.com/former-first-deputy-governor-of-bog-chairs-ecobank-board/ - a former First Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana chairing the Ecobank board, which would be a move out of the central bank into a listed banking group and is a different episode from the Matilda Asante-Asiedu record filed here. Also unopened: bog.gov.gh/governance/, the Bank of Ghana's own governance page, which should carry the deputy governors' career histories and would settle the Access Bank leg in the bank's own words.

GHA/IND ownership gap: no source was found in budget that states the ownership of Access Bank (Ghana) PLC or describes HDFC Bank Limited as a private sector bank. Both records are filed saying so. The cheap fix next round is the Ghana Stock Exchange or Access Bank Plc group structure page for the first, and HDFC Bank's annual report shareholding pattern or the RBI's own list of private sector banks for the second - one document each, settling the ownership leg in a primary source.

NZL: Harbour Asset Management's ownership is stated by neither the RBNZ release nor the Investment News report. Harbour's own site or a Financial Markets Authority disclosure would settle it. A second New Zealand candidate was identified from the same RBNZ release and not pursued: Simone Robbers, appointed Assistant Governor from 18 February 2019, whom the release describes as coming from the NZ Financial Markets Authority (a public regulator, so the move itself is public) after earlier private-sector roles in banking and wealth management that the release does not name - naming them would need a second source.

SGP: the HSBC biography exists as a series of dated PDF versions on hsbc.com (files/hsbc/who-we-are/leadership/biography/*-biography-swee-lian-teo.pdf, several dates), which may carry fuller MAS dates than the HTML page. Not opened. Also unopened: theedgesingapore's report that UOB appointed a former MAS deputy managing director of financial supervision, which may be the Ong Chong Tee episode the map already holds rather than a new one, and OCBC's own director page for Andrew Khoo.

KHM: the remaining ACLEDA ff_bod_* and ff_mgt_* biography pages (Rath Yumeng, Heng Dyna, Kay Lot, In Channy, Van Sou Ieng and others) are one dated CV per person on the host that produced the existing Cambodian record, and only one of them was read.

Twenty-two of the 29 assigned places were not touched at all for want of budget: ABW, BDI, BLR, CHN, COG, CRI, DZA, ETH, GNQ, LBR, MKD, MWI, PNG, SGP aside, SOM, SWZ, TUN, VEN and the rest. CHN is the largest untried one on this row and the hard case: the plausible destinations for former People's Bank of China officials are state-controlled (the big four commercial banks, CICC, the policy banks and Central Huijin), so a counted Chinese record needs a source stating private or mixed ownership on its face, and no search was spent on it this round.
